precepts.text: Every one that was in distress, in debt, and discontented gathered themselves unto David, and he became a captain over them, about four hundred men. The beginning of IUIC was men with problems and issues, not the full package, taken in and built with structure and discipline, as the women are built through Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2, and Daughters of Sarah. 2 Samuel 17:8: thy father and his men be mighty men, chafed in their minds as a bear robbed of her whelps. Not mighty at first; David put in the work, as the leadership put work in us.
precepts.point: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Evil communications come to men and women, and when they come you shut them down and do not entertain them, as the captain was drilling, or you end up caught in foolishness. A father who came up through this will make sure his sons learn that discipline and are not given feminine softness, so that when he grows up he can deal with a woman properly. That is not abuse.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

precepts.why:
“And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.”

The men who gathered to David were not the full package. They were in distress, in debt and discontented: men with problems and issues. David took them in and became a captain over them. That was the beginning of IUIC too: men with problems and issues, taken in and built with structure and discipline. The women are built the same way, through Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2 and Daughters of Sarah.

Later those same men are spoken of differently. In 2 Samuel 17:8 Hushai says to Absalom, “thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field.” They were not mighty at first. David put in the work, the same way the leadership put the work in us.

That is why it sits with “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” Everyone comes in with negative impulses, and we expect it. Hard times create warriors against sinful impulses, and the men are the vanguards of righteousness, to ward off any semblance of sin. When evil communications come to men and women, you shut them down and do not entertain them. The ones who come in get tried and watched, and the demons get exercised out of them through the congregation, the brothers and sisters that are watching them. If you really want to get yourself right, you will thank them for the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. But if you refuse to change, you have to go, because we cannot let a bad example destroy the rest of the flock.

precepts.text: Never trust thine enemy; but Saul had placed an Edomite over his servants.
precepts.point: The scriptures tell us we are never supposed to trust our enemies, yet what we are reading is Saul with an Edomite set over his servants.
precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” The scriptures tell us we are never supposed to trust our enemies, yet here is Saul with an Edomite set over his servants.

“Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul.” He reported that he “saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub”, and that Ahimelech “enquired of the Lord for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.” Saul had placed his enemy over his own house, and that enemy's wickedness came out.

precepts.text: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and purposed in his heart to slay his brother; Rebekah warned Jacob that Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee. That comfort in killing is the spirit seen again in Doeg the Edomite.
precepts.point: Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us; when Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests.
precepts.why:
“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” Rebekah warned Jacob: “Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.”

Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. That comfort in killing is the spirit seen again in Doeg the Edomite.

Saul told his footmen, “Turn, and slay the priests of the Lord”, but “the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord.” Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do. “Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod”, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, “both men and women, children and sucklings.”

Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us. When Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it, and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests.

points: So we see what happened: Saul accused Ahimelech and the priests of conspiracy. After that, Doeg killed 85 priests, and the city of Nob was destroyed. All because of hatred and envy.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Notice here, Saul became so desperate that he interpreted the loyalty to David as a betrayal to himself, because he wanted everybody against King David. Same thing we see today. No new thing under the sun: where people will put slander out to try to turn whole congregations to hate a man that they have never seen. Bishop Nathanyel never sat down with these brothers, broke bread. These are new Johnny come lately brothers, fresh out the pamper brothers. But they hate a man that they have not set with. They don't know his history. They know nothing. But because of hatred, that's what they do.
